name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH12_MATCH_Q01 - Bt toxin genes and insect specificity

questiontext.text:
Match the Bt-related terms in the left list with their correct descriptions in the right list:

List IList II
(1) cryIAc and cryIIAb(i) Solubilisation and activation of Bt protoxin
(2) cryIAb(ii) Control of cotton bollworms
(3) Bacillus thuringiensis(iii) Source of insecticidal crystal proteins
(4) Alkaline gut pH(iv) Control of corn borer

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bacillus thuringiensis produces crystalline insecticidal proteins (Bt toxins) encoded by cry genes. These toxins exist as inactive protoxins in the bacterium and become active only under specific insect gut conditions.

Step 2: Direct Concept Pairing
The genes cryIAc and cryIIAb encode proteins that specifically control cotton bollworms. The gene cryIAb encodes a protein that controls corn borer. Bacillus thuringiensis is the bacterial source that produces these insecticidal crystal proteins during a particular growth phase. The alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilises the ingested crystals and converts the inactive protoxin into the active toxin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: cryIAc and cryIIAb with control of cotton bollworms; cryIAb with control of corn borer; Bacillus thuringiensis with source of insecticidal crystal proteins; and alkaline gut pH with solubilisation and activation of Bt protoxin.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH12_MATCH_Q02 - GM crops and agricultural benefits

questiontext.text:
Match the genetically modified crop applications in the left list with their corresponding outcomes in the right list:

List IList II
(1) Golden rice(i) Prevents early exhaustion of soil fertility
(2) Nematode-resistant tobacco(ii) Enhanced nutritional value with Vitamin A
(3) Bt cotton(iii) Pest resistance without chemical insecticides
(4) Increased mineral usage efficiency(iv) Host-generated dsRNA silences parasite mRNA

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Genetically modified (GM) plants have been engineered to improve crop nutrition, confer pest resistance, reduce reliance on chemical pesticides, and optimise soil resource use.

Step 2: Direct Concept Pairing
Golden rice is a Vitamin A-enriched rice variety demonstrating enhanced nutritional value of food. Nematode-resistant tobacco uses RNA interference (RNAi), where host-generated double-stranded RNA silences the specific mRNA of Meloidogyne incognita. Bt cotton expresses bacterial toxin genes to act as a bio-pesticide, providing pest resistance without chemical insecticides. Increased efficiency of mineral usage by GM plants prevents early exhaustion of soil fertility.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: Golden rice with enhanced nutritional value with Vitamin A; nematode-resistant tobacco with host-generated dsRNA silencing parasite mRNA; Bt cotton with pest resistance without chemical insecticides; and increased mineral usage efficiency with preventing early exhaustion of soil fertility.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH12_MATCH_Q03 - Genetically engineered human insulin production

questiontext.text:
Match the insulin-related items in the left list with their correct characteristics in the right list:

List IList II
(1) Pro-insulin(i) Chains A and B linked by disulphide bridges
(2) Mature insulin(ii) Contains an extra C-peptide stretch
(3) Eli Lilly (1983)(iii) Caused allergy or immune reactions in some patients
(4) Animal-source insulin(iv) Prepared separate DNA sequences for A and B chains in E. coli

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Human insulin is synthesised as an inactive precursor (pro-hormone) that undergoes processing to form the active hormone, and recombinant DNA technology enabled its safe mass production in bacteria.

Step 2: Direct Concept Pairing
Pro-insulin contains an extra polypeptide stretch called the C-peptide, which is removed during maturation. Mature insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, chain A and chain B, linked together by disulphide bridges. In 1983, Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains of human insulin and introduced them into E. coli plasmids to produce the chains separately before combining them via disulphide bonds. Insulin extracted earlier from slaughtered cattle and pigs caused allergy or other immune reactions to the foreign protein in some patients.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: Pro-insulin with containing an extra C-peptide stretch; mature insulin with chains A and B linked by disulphide bridges; Eli Lilly (1983) with preparing separate DNA sequences for A and B chains in E. coli; and animal-source insulin with causing allergy or immune reactions in some patients.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH12_MATCH_Q04 - Gene therapy and molecular diagnostics

questiontext.text:
Match the medical biotechnology techniques and disorders in the left list with their descriptions in the right list:

List IList II
(1) ADA deficiency(i) Based on antigen–antibody interaction
(2) Retroviral vector(ii) Amplifies low-concentration pathogen nucleic acid
(3) PCR(iii) Introduces functional ADA cDNA into lymphocytes
(4) ELISA(iv) Treated by bone marrow transplantation or enzyme replacement

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biotechnological applications in medicine include gene therapy for hereditary disorders and molecular diagnostic tools for early disease detection.

Step 2: Direct Concept Pairing
Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, caused by deletion of the ADA gene, can be treated in some children by bone marrow transplantation or enzyme replacement therapy (though neither is completely curative). A retroviral vector is used in gene therapy to introduce functional ADA cDNA into cultured patient lymphocytes. Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) detects very low concentrations of bacteria or viruses before symptoms appear by amplifying their nucleic acids. Enzyme Linked Immuno-sorbent Assay (ELISA) operates on the principle of antigen–antibody interaction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: ADA deficiency with bone marrow transplantation or enzyme replacement; retroviral vector with introducing functional ADA cDNA into lymphocytes; PCR with amplifying low-concentration pathogen nucleic acid; and ELISA with antigen–antibody interaction.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH12_MATCH_Q05 - Transgenic animals and human welfare applications

questiontext.text:
Match the transgenic animal products and models in the left list with their specific uses in the right list:

List IList II
(1) Human α-1-antitrypsin(i) Could replace monkeys for batch safety testing
(2) Rosie (transgenic cow)(ii) Obtains toxicity testing results in less time
(3) Transgenic mice for polio vaccine(iii) Used to treat emphysema
(4) Toxin-sensitive transgenic animals(iv) Milk containing human alpha-lactalbumin (2.4 g/L)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Transgenic animals are engineered to carry and express foreign genes for producing biological therapeutics, testing vaccine safety, and conducting chemical toxicity evaluations.

Step 2: Direct Concept Pairing
Human α-1-antitrypsin is a biological product produced via transgenic animals to treat emphysema. Rosie, the first transgenic cow (1997), produced milk enriched with human alpha-lactalbumin at 2.4 grams per litre. Transgenic mice are used to test the safety of the polio vaccine and, if reliable, could replace monkeys for batch safety testing. Transgenic animals engineered to carry genes making them more sensitive to toxic substances allow chemical safety (toxicity) testing results to be obtained in less time.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: human α-1-antitrypsin with treatment of emphysema; Rosie with milk containing human alpha-lactalbumin (2.4 g/L); transgenic mice for polio vaccine with replacing monkeys for batch safety testing; and toxin-sensitive transgenic animals with obtaining toxicity testing results in less time.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH12_MATCH_Q06 - Ethical issues GEAC and biopiracy

questiontext.text:
Match the ethical and regulatory terms in the left list with their correct descriptions in the right list:

List IList II
(1) GEAC(i) Unauthorised use of bio-resources without compensatory payment
(2) Basmati rice patent (1997)(ii) Decides validity of GM research and safety of GM organisms
(3) Biopiracy(iii) Addresses patent terms, emergency provisions, and R&D initiatives
(4) Second amendment of Indian Patents Bill(iv) US patent on a variety derived from Indian farmer varieties

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Regulation of genetic modification and protection of biodiversity and traditional knowledge against unauthorised commercial exploitation are key ethical issues in biotechnology.

Step 2: Direct Concept Pairing
The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC) was set up by the Indian Government to make decisions regarding the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM organisms for public services. In 1997, an American company obtained US patent rights on a variety of Basmati rice derived from Indian farmer varieties crossed with semi-dwarf varieties. Biopiracy refers to the use of bio-resources by multinational companies and other organisations without proper authorisation and without compensatory payment. The second amendment of the Indian Patents Bill takes such issues into consideration, including patent terms, emergency provisions, and research and development initiatives.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: GEAC with deciding validity of GM research and safety of GM organisms; Basmati rice patent (1997) with US patent on a variety derived from Indian farmer varieties; biopiracy with unauthorised use of bio-resources without compensatory payment; and second amendment of Indian Patents Bill with addressing patent terms, emergency provisions, and R&D initiatives.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH12_MATCH_Q07 - Integrated biotechnology concepts and mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Match the biotechnological concepts in the left list with their correct mechanistic or functional descriptions in the right list:

List IList II
(1) Radioactive probe and autoradiography(i) Studying gene regulation and normal body development
(2) Agrobacterium vector in RNAi(ii) Mutated gene clone fails to appear on photographic film
(3) Insulin-like growth factor transgenic model(iii) Best catalyst, optimal conditions, and downstream processing
(4) Critical research areas of biotechnology(iv) Introduces DNA producing both sense and anti-sense RNA

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Modern biotechnology integrates core engineering principles, molecular hybridisation diagnostics, vector-mediated gene silencing, and transgenic physiological studies.

Step 2: Direct Concept Pairing
When a radioactive single-stranded DNA or RNA probe is hybridised to cellular clones and detected by autoradiography, a clone carrying a mutated gene fails to appear on the photographic film because the probe lacks complementarity with the mutated gene. In RNA interference against nematodes, Agrobacterium vectors introduce DNA designed to produce both sense and anti-sense RNA in the host plant. Transgenic animals altered for insulin-like growth factor help researchers study gene regulation and normal physiological development. The three critical research areas of biotechnology are providing the best catalyst, creating optimal engineering conditions, and downstream processing technologies.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matches are: radioactive probe and autoradiography with mutated gene clone failing to appear on photographic film; Agrobacterium vector in RNAi with introducing DNA producing both sense and anti-sense RNA; insulin-like growth factor transgenic model with studying gene regulation and normal body development; and critical research areas of biotechnology with best catalyst, optimal conditions, and downstream processing.
